papers.title: Optimized machine learning models for personalized organ dose prediction in whole-body
papers.abstract: This study investigates the use of machine learning (ML) models to improve the accuracy of organ dose prediction in whole-body Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography (PET/CT) imaging using the 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) radiotracer. Nine ML models: Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), Ensemble Methods (ENS), Stepwise Linear Regression (SLR), Efficient Linear Regression (ELR), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Efficient Linear Regression (ELR), Tree Regression (TR), Kernel Approximation Regression (KAR), and Neural Networks (NN), were evaluated and validated based on their ability to predict organ dose based on demographic parameters such as weight, height, age, and organ function. The results revealed that the best-performing model was highly dependent on the specific organ and patient gender. The optimized Gaussian Process Regression with Bayesian Optimization (GPR+BO) model showed strong performance, particularly for the male brain (R² = 0.91) and gallbladder (R² = 0.94). However, the Ensemble (ENS) model demonstrated superior or equivalent performance for other organs in male patients, including the kidneys (R² = 0.94) and lungs (R² = 0.95). For female patients, model performance also varied, with the NN+BO model showing the best predictive accuracy for the liver (R² = 0.93). Gender-based analysis indicated that female patients absorbed higher organ doses despite similar radiotracer levels, with notable differences observed in the brain (0.36 ± 0.05 mGy for females vs. 0.33 ± 0.05 mGy for males) and lungs (0.22 ± 0.03 mGy for females vs. 0.18 ± 0.03 mGy for males). These findings show the importance of adjusting radiotracer doses based on physiological variations to ensure accurate, patient-specific dose management. This study uniquely integrates GPR+BO, significantly enhancing predictive accuracy and potentially improving patient safety by enabling personalized radiation dose in clinical PET/CT procedures

papers.title: The Impact of Team Based Learning in Learning Outcome of Pharmacology Among II MBBS Students
papers.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of Team-Based Learning (TBL) in improving learning outcomes among second-year MBBS students in Pharmacology. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among second-year MBBS students at Government Medical College, Nagapattinam. Students were oriented to the TBL process and informed of the learning objectives related to antianginal drugs. The TBL session, comprising Individual Readiness Assurance Test (IRAT), Team Readiness Assurance Test (TRAT), immediate feedback, and clinical problem-solving exercises, was conducted over a three-hour period following pre-class preparation. A delayed post-test (Delayed IRAT) was administered 10 d later to assess knowledge retention. Student feedback on TBL was collected using a validated 17-item Likert scale questionnaire. Data were analysed using the Friedman test followed by Wilcoxon signed-rank test for pairwise comparisons. Results: With the Sample size of 141, using Friedman test, there is statistically significant difference in student scores across the three point times: IRAT (mean Rank = 1.05), TRAT (2.33), and Delayed IRAT (2.63); p<0.001. Post-hoc analysis using Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Tests showed significant improvements between: IRAT vs TRAT (p<0.001), TRAT vs Delayed IRAT (p = 0.002), IRAT vs Delayed IRAT (p<0.001). Conclusion: Team-Based Learning significantly improved immediate learning outcomes and knowledge retention among second-year MBBS students. The strategy also enhanced student engagement, teamwork, and confidence in applying pharmacological concepts. Incorporating TBL into the undergraduate pharmacology curriculum may promote active learning and better achievement of competency-based medical education objectives.

papers.title: Berberine-Loaded Mesoporous Bioactive Glass Enhances Bone Repair through Combined Immunomodulatory and Osteogenic Effects.
papers.abstract: Bone repair is dependent on both local inflammatory control and osteogenic activity. In this study, berberine-loaded mesoporous bioactive glass (BG) nanoparticles (BG@Ber) were prepared to combine the osteogenic properties of mesoporous BG with the anti-inflammatory activity of berberine. The results showed that berberine was successfully loaded into the mesoporous glass without changing its amorphous structure and could be released over time. BG@Ber also showed good hemocompatibility and cytocompatibility in vitro. Compared with BG alone, BG@Ber showed a stronger regulatory effect on macrophage responses and further promoted osteogenic differentiation and mineralization in vitro. In a rat femoral condyle defect model, BG@Ber resulted in better bone formation and osseointegration with no obvious pathological abnormalities in major organs. Overall, berberine loading improved the biological performance of the mesoporous BG and was associated with better bone repair in vivo.
